project: Catholic Institutional AI Risk & Control Evidence Pilot
short_title: A Catholic institutional AI risk study
tagline: From documented technical risks to evidence of institutional control.
status: Development release: source-verification pilot started; independent research gates remain open
lead: This study asks a specific question: when a Catholic institution uses AI, what evidence would justify confidence that a relevant safeguard actually worked?
scope_statement: Begin with pastoral and catechetical AI assistants and Catholic educational systems. Treat healthcare, charity operations, and diocesan administration as possible later extensions, subject to research review.
warning: One bounded source-verification run is recorded. Its two selected search/fetch pairs did not yield their requested verified passages. Eighteen normative mappings remain unreviewed; zero Catholic empirical cases are admitted and no Catholic safeguard evaluation is completed.
north_star: A documented risk is a reason to investigate. It is not proof that harm occurred. A written safeguard is a claim. Its effectiveness must be supported by evidence.

current.label: Source-verification run
current.note: Two targets; four MCP calls; no retries

targets.label: Incident records
targets.note: Direct Catholic and external analogues kept distinct

targets.label: Controlled evaluations
targets.note: Frozen test methods and retained negative results

primary_question: Can a source-traceable, event-control evidence method improve the support and reproducibility of AI risk and safeguard assessments in Catholic institutional settings, compared with simpler narrative and checklist representations?
contribution: A bounded, testable crosswalk connecting general AI failure mechanisms, Catholic institutional workflows, source-located obligations, candidate controls, and what independent reviewers can establish from surviving evidence. The added value must be demonstrated against simpler representations.
alternative: A source-linked narrative or a clear checklist may achieve comparable reconstruction with much less effort. If so, the additional CEC structure must be narrowed or justified by another measured benefit.

hypotheses.title: Better-supported reconstruction
hypotheses.claim: CEC-style event-control records will reduce unsupported categorical conclusions against an uncertainty-aware narrative and checklist, when all reviewers receive identical source material.
hypotheses.measure: Unsupported yes/no conclusions per applicable control opportunity; also unresolved-state retention, traceability and reviewer burden.
hypotheses.challenge: Comparable outcomes at lower cost for simpler representations would disconfirm practical advantage.

hypotheses.title: Reliable Catholic contextualization
hypotheses.claim: Independent technical and qualified Catholic reviewers can consistently identify which institutional obligations and workflows are implicated by a documented technical risk.
hypotheses.measure: Independent agreement, retained disagreements, unclassifiable cases and revision costs.
hypotheses.challenge: Unstable categories or interpretive disagreements may make the crosswalk unsuitable for empirical use.

hypotheses.title: Testable safeguard response
hypotheses.claim: A specified candidate safeguard reduces a frozen failure outcome against a defined baseline within a controlled test setting.
hypotheses.measure: Observed failures, missed benign requests, false positives, invalid responses and uncertainty across conditions.
hypotheses.challenge: Inconsistent, trivial, or context-dependent differences limit assurance claims.

hypotheses.title: What public evidence cannot settle
hypotheses.claim: Some institutional control questions remain unresolved because reports omit configuration, authority, deployment or downstream records.
hypotheses.measure: Counts of unknown, not reported, not observable and conflicting states under a fixed retrieval procedure.
hypotheses.challenge: Cannot infer actual absence of a safeguard from missing records.

pipeline.title: Discover
pipeline.subtitle: Existing homepage map
pipeline.description: MIT risk records, incident candidates and governance links. These are discovery inputs, not validated study cases.

pipeline.title: Screen
pipeline.subtitle: Catholic relevance and source rights
pipeline.description: Retain raw IDs, snapshot dates, exclusion reasons, source dependence, technical mechanism and institutional context.

pipeline.title: Review
pipeline.subtitle: Independent expert judgment
pipeline.description: Review source-located paragraphs against the original Vatican text; separate retrieval metadata, technical classification, and Catholic normative interpretation. Preserve disagreement.

pipeline.title: Reconstruct
pipeline.subtitle: CEC evidence workbench
pipeline.description: For eligible cases, record each event, control opportunity, supporting claim and unresolved state.

pipeline.title: Evaluate
pipeline.subtitle: Controlled experiments
pipeline.description: Compare baseline and safeguard conditions using frozen tests; retain raw results, invalid outputs and negative controls.

pipeline.title: Report
pipeline.subtitle: Versioned, bounded findings
pipeline.description: Update the study report with reviewed evidence, explicit limits, author sign-off and correction history.

audiences.title: Catholic leaders
audiences.copy: What decision would a bishop, school leader or ministry director face? What can be established? What must remain with a qualified person?

audiences.title: Theologians and canonists
audiences.copy: Which document or canon is relevant, what exactly does it say, and which applied interpretation still needs expert review?

audiences.title: Researchers and evaluators
audiences.copy: Can another team reproduce the screening, annotations, comparisons, tests and limits from versioned materials?

objects.name: Risk scenario
objects.question: What could fail?
objects.body: A defined technical mechanism in a specific Catholic institutional workflow. Does not establish that harm occurred.

objects.name: Incident record
objects.question: What was reported?
objects.body: An attributed event with preserved source, uncertainty, and direct or analogous relevance. Does not prove the proposed cause.

objects.name: Normative mapping
objects.question: What duty is relevant?
objects.body: Source-located teaching, canon law or institutional guidance plus a separately identified interpretation.

objects.name: Control observation
objects.question: Did a safeguard operate?
objects.body: CEC event × control objective × opportunity × period. Makes missing evidence and claimed effect visible.

objects.name: Controlled evaluation
objects.question: What happened in a test?
objects.body: Predeclared conditions, baselines, perturbations, observed outputs, negative controls and limitations.

first_case.title: Illustrative case: a parish AI assistant
first_case.disclaimer: Hypothetical scenario for explaining the method. No new real-world incident or evaluation result is claimed.
first_case.risk: An assistant implies that it possesses priestly or sacramental authority.
first_case.setting: A parish uses a chatbot for general faith questions and service information.
first_case.evidence: Product behavior and system records would be required; public reporting alone may establish only a claim or analogous event.
first_case.norm: A reviewer consults precise ecclesial sources and records the applicability judgment separately.
first_case.control: Proposed disclosure and escalation rules, with restrictions on personification and sacramental claims.
first_case.test: Frozen prompts probe authority claims, with benign controls and human review of outputs.
first_case.limit: Passing a synthetic test cannot certify pastoral safety, doctrinal fidelity or deployment suitability.

stages.subtitle: Define the question before data selection
actions: Protocol 0.3.0 includes a bounded source-verification amendment; the main comparison remains unfrozen.

stages.subtitle: Use existing ingestion rather than repeat it

stages.name: Catholic crosswalk feasibility
stages.subtitle: Test the first five scenarios
actions: Map technical mechanisms to two institutional settings
Separate canonical sources from researcher interpretations
Obtain independent technical and qualified Catholic review
Verify Magisterium-retrieved passage IDs and Vatican paragraph locators before source admission
stages.deliverable: Five reviewed pilot crosswalk records and disagreement report
stages.gate: G2 · Category definitions revised and frozen only after feasibility review

stages.name: Comparative reconstruction
stages.subtitle: Test CEC against simpler views
actions: Prepare identical evidence packets in three representations
Independently enumerate controls before scoring
Measure unsupported claims, uncertainty retention and burden
stages.deliverable: Blinded comparative pilot design and annotated results
stages.gate: G3 · Methods and acceptance thresholds locked before primary comparison
stages.dependency: Requires source packets, rubric and independent assessors

stages.name: Reproducible safeguard tests
stages.subtitle: Study 3–5 bounded failure mechanisms
actions: Freeze baseline and intervention conditions
Specify benign controls, perturbations and failure criteria
Preserve responses, rejected outputs, adjudications and versions
stages.deliverable: Experiment packages, results, uncertainty and failure register
stages.gate: G4 · Reproducibility and test validity review
stages.dependency: Requires prepared protocols and systems under test

stages.name: Synthesis and research review
stages.subtitle: Separate findings from interpretation
actions: Report the positive, negative and unresolved findings
Assess validity, source coverage, selection bias and limitations
Prepare reproducible companion and independent review dossier
stages.deliverable: Study report, notebook, versioned data products and corrections
stages.gate: G5 · Research-integrity, rights and independent-release approval

stages.name: External discussion
stages.subtitle: Bring evidence, not an unsupported claim
actions: Assess CDCF C1–C8 internally and label as self-assessment
Clarify ownership, IP and conflicts before submission
Invite critique from CDCF and Leonum without implying endorsement
stages.deliverable: Bounded reviewer briefing and open-question register
stages.gate: G6 · Written scope of external review and institutional relationship
stages.dependency: Requires at least a defensible pilot report

comparison.name: Source-linked narrative
comparison.what: Readable case narrative with citations and explicit uncertainty, using the same evidence.

comparison.name: Uncertainty-aware checklist
comparison.what: Control checklist retaining unknown, not reported, and non-applicable states.

comparison.name: CEC event-control record
comparison.what: Control opportunity, evidence item, source origin, action, propagation, and bounded inference.

boundaries.title: Risk ≠ incident
boundaries.copy: A risk record describes a possible failure. Incident evidence concerns a reported event.

boundaries.title: Source count ≠ independence
boundaries.copy: Repeated reporting of one institutional assertion does not create new independent evidence.

boundaries.title: Policy ≠ operation
boundaries.copy: A written safeguard alone does not establish that it affected a decision.

boundaries.title: Catholic relevance ≠ doctrinal judgment
boundaries.copy: Normative applicability needs precise sources and appropriately qualified review.

boundaries.title: Synthetic ≠ deployed
boundaries.copy: Laboratory test outcomes do not establish effectiveness in a parish, school or diocese.

boundaries.title: Missing evidence ≠ failure
boundaries.copy: A report that says nothing about a control cannot prove the control was absent.

boundaries.title: AI citation ≠ verified original
boundaries.copy: A returned passage ID or search link is not accepted until the fetched locator and original Vatican paragraph agree.
